You are a blind semantic decoder. The inline crystal document in the user message is your only material-specific source. Check that its natural-language spatial claims agree with the typed values and public crystallographic rules. If prose, tags, and public rules conflict, return status="conflict" and identify the contradiction; do not silently privilege a false sentence or repair it. Do not use external retrieval, infer missing facts, repair values, or assume a default for any field. Return exactly one JSON object, with no Markdown fences.

For a complete, consistent description return status="ok" and exactly these keys: status, space_group_number, hall_symbol, lattice (six input-cell values in a,b,c,alpha,beta,gamma order), input_atom_count, composition (element-to-positive-integer counts), orbits (objects with id, element, wyckoff, and parameters), frame_transform (matrix and origin_shift), round_digits (integer or null), and precision_corrections (objects with site_id, element, and a three-number input-frame fractional delta). Orbit parameters follow the public table's listed free-axis order; do not substitute a fitted equivalent representative. Preserve every number and identifier exactly as tagged. Keep distinct same-element orbits distinct.

If facts are absent or contradictory, return only {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."} or {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}.

The crystal is described in space group number <param name="space_group.number" type="int" unit="identifier" frame="public">139</param>, with the Hall symbol <param name="space_group.hall" type="string" unit="Hall_symbol" frame="public">"-I 4 2"</param>. The input structure contains <param name="input.atom_count" type="int" unit="atom" frame="input">3</param> atoms in total, comprising <param name="composition.Kr" type="composition_count" unit="atom" frame="input">{"element":"Kr","count":1}</param> and <param name="composition.F" type="composition_count" unit="atom" frame="input">{"element":"F","count":2}</param>.

The original input cell is specified by lattice parameters <param name="cell.a" type="float64" unit="angstrom" frame="input">4.55223999</param>, <param name="cell.b" type="float64" unit="angstrom" frame="input">4.55223999</param>, and <param name="cell.c" type="float64" unit="angstrom" frame="input">4.55223999</param>, with interaxial angles <param name="cell.alpha" type="float64" unit="degree" frame="input">122.44045171</param>, <param name="cell.beta" type="float64" unit="degree" frame="input">122.44045171</param>, and <param name="cell.gamma" type="float64" unit="degree" frame="input">85.82255785</param>. This input cell is transformed into the standard crystallographic frame using the matrix <param name="frame.matrix" type="float64[3,3]" unit="1" frame="standard_from_input">[[0.5,-0.5,0.5],[-0.5,0.5,0.5],[-0.5,-0.5,0.5]]</param> together with the origin shift <param name="frame.origin_shift" type="float64[3]" unit="fractional" frame="standard">[0.0,0.0,0.0]</param>. Fractional coordinates in the input description are rounded to <param name="round_digits" type="null|int" unit="decimal_places" frame="input_fractional">6</param> decimal places.

In the standard frame, the independent atomic content is represented by two Wyckoff orbits. The krypton atoms occupy orbit <param name="orbit.o000.id" type="string" unit="orbit_identifier" frame="public_expansion">"o000"</param>, with element <param name="orbit.o000.element" type="string" unit="element" frame="orbit">"Kr"</param> on Wyckoff position <param name="orbit.o000.wyckoff" type="string" unit="Wyckoff_label" frame="public_table">"2a"</param>. The fluorine atoms occupy orbit <param name="orbit.o001.id" type="string" unit="orbit_identifier" frame="public_expansion">"o001"</param>, with element <param name="orbit.o001.element" type="string" unit="element" frame="orbit">"F"</param> on Wyckoff position <param name="orbit.o001.wyckoff" type="string" unit="Wyckoff_label" frame="public_table">"4e"</param>, and this orbit carries the free coordinate <param name="orbit.o001.parameters" type="float64[1]" unit="fractional" frame="standard">[0.2904070000000001]</param>. No precision corrections are supplied, so the description contains no additional deviations from the idealized backbone beyond the stated structural parameters.
